title: Type Routing Decision Tree
description: A Mermaid flowchart of the generator skill's routing decision tree: thirteen yes-or-no questions about an objective's data shape, asked in order and stopping at the first yes, each yes ending in a leaf naming the MicroSim type and library, with a custom p5.js simulation when every answer is no. Every node has a click directive that opens an explanation and an example objective, and a Try an objective mode routes six objectives and compares the learner's path with the tree's.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Educational Technology
Instructional Design
MicroSim Engineering
Decision Trees

educational.audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners
educational.topic: Routing a learning objective to a MicroSim type
learningObjectives: The learner will use the routing questions to select the correct MicroSim type for six described objectives.
prerequisites: Classifying an objective by Bloom level and verb
The idea of a data shape

accessibility.notes: Node text is real HTML inside the SVG; explanations appear as plain HTML in the infobox.

controls.label: Clear my path
controls.action: Remove the learner's path for the current objective

controls.label: Any node
controls.action: Show its explanation and example; in Try mode, choose where the learner stops

simulation.modelType: Ordered decision tree with path comparison
assumptions: Question order follows the specification, which takes it from the decision tree in the generator skill's SKILL.md.
limitations: The skill's tree also has celebration-effects and HTML-matrix questions; the specification folds the matrix into the comparison-table question and omits celebration effects.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Guided practice applying an ordered procedure, with immediate path comparison
keyQuestions: What is the data shape of this objective?
Which question does it answer yes to first?
When could two questions both fairly answer yes?
commonMisconceptions: Any question that fits can be chosen; the order does not matter.
A keyword such as 'map' always means a geographic map.
If no standard library fits, the objective cannot be built.
assessmentOpportunities: First-try routing accuracy on the six objectives
Written reasons for each 'no' above the stopping question
